knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The footing depth comes from the approved design and the ground conditions. A change is referred, not made on site, as the footings section of this lesson sets out.
A post is loaded only after the concrete has cured for the period recorded from the supplier and the design.
The service plan must be checked and responses on file before excavation, and the work stops if services are found [BYDA-DUTY].

practicalCriteria: In a supervised setting, sets a training post to a design height and plumb reference, braces it, and records plumb and level readings within the tolerance on the sample drawing.
Completes a service-check record for a sample excavation, showing the plan request, asset owner responses and the stop point if a service is found.
Writes a referral for a sample design change (for example, a footing depth that cannot be reached), without changing the depth on site.
passRule: Assessor observation of the supervised post set and review of the service-check record and referral, with all three practical criteria met against the sample design. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Footing and post-setting record with readings
Service-check record with plan reference and responses
Photographs of the set post before backfilling, in a supervised setting
Referral note for the design change, with the reply
stopWorkCriteria: Services are found or suspected, and digging continues
A footing depth or post size is changed on site without a written referral
A post is loaded before its recorded cure time has passed
A brace is removed before the concrete has set, or a post is forced into line
